request.spec:
Show on each person the due of their OPEN and PENDING claims that count, split by the age of
the claim on the sheet's today (the days from the claim's date): aged 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60, and
61 or more. A claim dated after today counts as 0 to 30.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person the due of their OPEN and PENDING claims that count, split by the age of
the claim on the sheet's today (the days from the claim's date): aged 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60, and
61 or more. A claim dated after today counts as 0 to 30.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows how much is due on their OPEN and PENDING claims, split by age: 0–30 days, 31–60 days and 61 or more. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

The change is one new file, `src/main/frontend/features/claims/aged.slot.tsx`, which adds three columns right after the Overdue columns:
- **What it adds up:** the same claims the due-total and overdue figures count. So claims that are deferred, held, or settled (or any status other than OPEN and PENDING) are left out.
- **Each claim's amount:** its due as the rest of the app works it out, including any late charge and the sheet's floor. Claims with no rate (n/a) are skipped.
- **Age:** the days from the claim's date to the sheet's today. A claim dated after today counts as 0, so it goes in 0–30.

The figures are worked out in the browser from data the screen already loads, the same way the existing overdue figures are. So there were no changes to the server or the stored data, and no new audit records.
